_note: All 185 concordia plates read on 47 sheets at 776 px (runs/qc/plate_sheets/concordia). No identifiable real face -- every human figure is a back, a silhouette or a distant figure. No legible glyph, no watermark, no wrong-country signage (the film IS set in Italy, so Italian architecture is correct here). Funnels checked at 1600 px on N183 and N147: plain white, NO company mark, so the yellow cast on some plates is sunset light and not a real operator's livery. CORRECTED 2026-08-26 from a first pass that rejected four plates as period drift: all four are ship's CLINOMETERS, which is the right instrument and the film's own motif -- a ship that lists. The fault is only the OPEN-FLAME OIL LANTERN the prompt put beside three of them. N116 has no lantern and is accepted.
reviewer: claude-design-thread 2026-08-26, plate sheets at 776 px, funnels at 1600 px

reject.N001: the clinometer is right and is the film's motif; the burning OIL LANTERN beside it is not. The Costa Concordia was delivered in 2006 and carries no open flame. This is the opening register, so the anachronism lands in the first seconds
reject.N104: same shoot, same fault: a lit oil lantern beside the clinometer, under a sentence about the 2012 passage
reject.N141: same fault, in the ENDING. The prompt's 'a bright brass lamp burning beside it' is what produces the lantern; the instrument itself is correct

note.N116: ACCEPTED, and it is the proof of what is wrong with the other three: same brass clinometer, no lantern in the prompt, no anachronism in the picture
note.N159: brass binnacle compass -- KEPT. A magnetic compass in a brass binnacle is genuine equipment on a modern ship
note.N157: brass ship's bell -- KEPT, for the same reason
note.N169: a wood-panelled study with a brass desk lamp. Period-styled but plausible as a ship's library; do not use it under a sentence about the bridge or the engine room
note.N091: a theatre audience seen from behind. No face resolves, but this is the densest crowd in the set -- if a downstream pass finds a face, look here first
note.N146: a muster line seen from behind, closest crowd to camera in the set. Same caution as N091
note.N139: a blank sign plate on a cabin door. Blank by design; if a later pass adds text it becomes a readable document
